title: Marvel Comics
subtitle: 13 reading orders
blurb: Thirteen Marvel reading orders as one list. Each row opens that order's own page, and finishing that page ticks the row here.
notes: Hover a row and a loupe appears with a fraction beside it — how far into that reading order you already are. Opening it takes you to its own page, an ordinary list with its own strip, its own schedule and its own clubs. Nothing about it changes because it is reachable from here.

Marking a row here ticks that whole order, and finishing that order marks the row here. Unticking a row only takes back the ticks this page put there — anything you had already marked yourself stays marked.
A mark's width is issues, not hours.

Comics publish no per-issue reading time, so there are no hours to size a mark with — but there are issues, and every Marvel list counts in them. Each door is drawn as wide as the number of issues in the order it opens, summed by the build out of that list's own rows rather than typed here, so a sixty-year spine reads wider than a three-year run. The count sits on the row as text as well.
Where these overlap, and where they do not.

Fantastic Four stops one issue short of Hickman, so it and Everything Dies meet without repeating a row. Spider-Man After Civil War starts where Amazing Spider-Man stops. An event list does cross several of these spines by design — that is what an event is — which is why ticking one list here never reaches into another. The three Spider-Man doors chain rather than overlap: Amazing Spider-Man stops at #528, Civil War carries #529-538, and After Civil War picks up at #539.
